items.title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
items.raw_content:
Authors: Mrityunjay Shukla, Shubham Roy, Biswabandan Panda

Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton. Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline. We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness. We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline. A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel. Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions. Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic. To identify exploitable bit-flip locations without manual inspection, we build Karnage, a tool that isolates useful bit-flip locations in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline. We evaluate LLVMHammer across a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Deepseek-llm-7B-chat, across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs. LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16\%, which, in turn, can translate into additional annual operating costs at the scale of multi-GPU deployments. We further show that LLVMhammer can also corrupt LLM outputs across different GPU vendors, reducing BERTScore to as low as 25\%, illustrating the broader security implications of bit-flips in Triton's compilation pipeline.
items.title_zh: 利用 Rowhammer 攻击放大 LLM 推理延迟与成本
items.summary: Researchers present LLVMhammer, a Rowhammer attack that flips a bit in Triton's compilation pipeline so it produces a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel, which is cached on disk and slows later runs. On NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs it raised single-GPU inference latency by 4-16% and could also corrupt outputs.

items.title: Evaluating the Applicability of LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon
items.raw_content:
Authors: Kyrylo Yemets, Andrii Yaroshevych, Victor Muryn, Ostap Khomenko, Pavlo Kryven et al.

Apple Silicon is among the most widely used platforms for local LLM inference, yet nearly all inference optimizations are designed and validated on server-class NVIDIA GPUs under batched serving workloads. Which optimizations retain their benefits when moved to Apple Silicon, and what determines their applicability? We evaluate four optimization families: KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported GPU kernels, and post-training quantization. Experiments span four Apple machines under a common single-request decode workload, with matched RTX 4090 comparisons where possible. KV-cache pruning can reach up to 1.75 times end-to-end throughput on Apple but can reduce throughput on desktop NVIDIA GPUs. Under the common benchmark, all evaluated speculative decoding methods reduce throughput on Apple, despite reported 2-6 times gains on server GPUs. CUDA kernel designs transfer only partially: public Metal lacks asynchronous copy, and batch-one decode makes several serving-oriented mechanisms inapplicable, although transferable components yield up to 1.20 times decode throughput. Quantization gains vary by machine. Across four families, a reported speedup is not a portable property of a technique alone but a joint function of technique, runtime, hardware contract, and workload regime.
items.title_zh: 评估 LLM 推理优化在 Apple Silicon 上的适用性
items.summary: A study evaluates KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported GPU kernels and post-training quantization on four Apple machines, finding that speedups reported on server NVIDIA GPUs often do not carry over; speculative decoding reduced throughput on Apple, while KV-cache pruning reached up to 1.75x.

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
items.raw_content:
Authors: Yunfei Xie, Howard H. Qian, Shiyi Lan, Kaiyu Hang, Chen Wei

Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.
items.title_zh: 感官运动对齐：衡量具身策略成功的柏拉图式代理指标
items.summary: The paper proposes Sensorimotor Alignment (S2), a training-free offline metric measuring how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion, and finds it correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families.

items.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Chenyuan Chen, Ran Ding, Lechen Zhang, Zewen He, Yoshihiko Nakamura

Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
items.title_zh: Memory before Goal：预历史记忆在人形机器人全身移动操作中的作用
items.summary: WholeBodyMem is an object-guided perceptual memory for whole-body vision-language-action policies that keeps key pre-history frames of task objects. It raised its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on a real Unitree G1, alongside a new HuMeGo benchmark.

items.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
items.raw_content:
Authors: Zecong Tang, Zian Guan, Yuncheng Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo et al.

Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
items.title_zh: HiSTEVE 1.0：面向开放世界游戏的人机界面 VLA 智能体
items.summary: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical VLA agent for Minecraft that pairs a VLM planner and structured memory with a single vision-only controller using native keyboard-and-mouse actions, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA.

items.title: PiHand: Latent Hand-Object Interaction Priors for Physics-Based Policy Learning
items.raw_content:
Authors: Niklas Berndt, Xianghui Xie, Enes Duran, Yixiao Wang, Gerard Pons-Moll

Synthesizing physically grounded dexterous hand-object interactions is important for VR/AR, gaming, and robotics, yet remains challenging because subtle contact dynamics, diverse object geometries, and target trajectories must be jointly respected while maintaining natural grasps. Existing methods either track mocap trajectories with limited transfer to novel objects, or rely on hand-only generative priors that fail to capture coupled hand-object motion, sacrificing contact fidelity and sample efficiency. To tackle these challenges, we introduce PiHand, a Physically grounded Interaction-aware Hand motion synthesis framework. PiHand first trains expert policies that track mocap demonstrations in simulation, distills them into a unified hand-object interaction prior using a goal-conditioned VAE, and finally solve diverse dexterous manipulation tasks through bounded residual exploration in its latent space. With only a single reward and no complex curriculum training, this yields general tabletop manipulation policies that generalize to unseen objects and trajectories on GRAB and DexYCB. The same prior transfers to object catching and bimanual handover, two tasks that are rarely seen in its training data. Across all tasks, PiHand consistently outperforms baselines in all metrics. We will release the processed data and model checkpoints.
items.title_zh: PiHand：基于物理的策略学习所需的潜在手物交互先验
items.summary: PiHand distills simulated expert policies that track mocap demonstrations into a goal-conditioned VAE prior over hand-object interaction, then solves dexterous manipulation tasks through bounded residual exploration, generalizing to unseen objects and trajectories on GRAB and DexYCB.

items.title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
items.raw_content:
Authors: Chao Gu, Quanyan Zhu

This paper studies the problem of safe tool execution for large language model (LLM) agents under prompt injection. Using Petri nets, we formalize the execution harness between the LLM and its tools as a supervisory control problem, in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets. Since a transition fires only if the marks it needs are present, an injected request whose preconditions are unmet or already spent is refused regardless of its wording. Treating tool outcomes as uncontrollable, we enforce safety by the conventional maximally permissive supervisor, and this safety transfers to the running system under four assumptions. Moreover, to capture an agent that may propose again after a refusal, we introduce the notion of a replanning closed loop, in which each retry costs an inference call. We show that, in this loop, the conventional supervisor can be arbitrarily more intrusive than a stricter safe one. Furthermore, for a given proposer model, the maximally permissive least-intrusive supervisor is characterized as a value-threshold refinement of the conventional one. Under precise conditions, this refinement orders two concurrent actions by at most one monitor place. On an autonomous release agent, we find by synthesis that safe deployment requires a step that the supervisor can refuse after a rollout starts.
items.title_zh: 面向 Agentic AI 的可认证执行框架：推理与行动之间的 Petri 网监督控制
items.summary: The paper models an LLM agent's tool-execution harness as a Petri-net supervisory control problem in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets, so an injected request with unmet preconditions is refused regardless of wording. It also analyzes a replanning loop in which each retry costs an inference call.

items.title: Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI
items.raw_content:
Authors: Claudia Giardina, Montse Pardàs, Verónica Vilaplana

Synthetic biparametric MRI (bpMRI) may help alleviate the limited availability of large and representative prostate MRI datasets for deep learning applications. In this work, we present a conditional 3D diffusion framework for anatomy-conditioned synthesis of complete prostate bpMRI from anatomical masks. The framework supports sequential synthesis, in which T2w and diffusion modalities are generated by separately trained models, and joint synthesis, in which all bpMRI modalities are generated simultaneously within a single model. Five configurations were trained using PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate, and PROSTATEx datasets to investigate different conditioning schemes, target modalities, and synthesis strategies. Evaluation using distribution-based metrics, paired-image similarity, and qualitative assessment demonstrated the feasibility of both synthesis pathways. Joint synthesis achieved competitive distributional fidelity while generating complete bpMRI, whereas direct synthesis of ADC and computed high-b-value DWI outperformed their derivation from synthetic diffusion-weighted images.
items.title_zh: 基于扩散模型合成完整三维双参数前列腺 MRI
items.summary: A conditional 3D diffusion framework synthesizes complete biparametric prostate MRI from anatomical masks, supporting both sequential and joint generation of T2w and diffusion modalities and trained on PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate and PROSTATEx.

items.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Jinyu Zhang, Haitao Lin, Jiashu Hou, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu

This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.
items.title_zh: F2G-Pose：面向 RGB-D 类别级物体姿态估计的几何感知基础特征提升
items.summary: F2G-Pose is a single-pass framework that predicts category-level object pose, metric size and camera-frame shape from one RGB-D observation by lifting visual foundation features to point clouds, running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference.

items.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
items.raw_content:
Authors: Aman Behera, Namit Solanki, Mehul Anand

Long-context models often use answer-bearing evidence less effectively when it appears away from a prompt boundary. We compare this position bias across Transformer, state-space, and hybrid Mamba architectures by moving one gold document through a fixed set of nine distractors. The evaluated Transformers show a beginning advantage that the evaluated state-space models lack, while both families favor evidence near the end. A matched pure-versus-hybrid Mamba comparison points in the same direction but remains statistically uncertain. The family difference appears among models that can answer the task. Transformer primacy reappears on synthetic retrieval, where state-space ceiling prevents a family comparison. A corpus swap within one state-space architecture changes overall accuracy without a detectable change in curve shape. Prompt changes can create or nearly remove a beginning advantage. Position remains decodable across architectures even when response curves differ, and attention concentration near initial tokens covaries with beginning sensitivity in the tested Transformer family. These exploratory results show that effective context use depends on the evaluated architecture family, capability, task, and prompt, without isolating the sequence mixer as the sole cause.
items.title_zh: Mixing Matters：长上下文问答中不同序列混合器的证据位置偏置
items.summary: The study moves one gold document through nine distractors to compare position bias across Transformer, state-space and hybrid Mamba models, finding that the tested Transformers show a beginning advantage the state-space models lack while both favor evidence near the end.

items.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
items.raw_content:
Authors: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Unai Zulaika, Ruben Sanchez-Corcuera, Aritz Bilbao-Jayo, Aitor Almeida

Accuracy on medical examinations is common evidence offered for the clinical use of language models, yet a health system that intends to run an open model on its own hardware needs to know considerably more: whether the model recognizes when it is likely to be wrong, whether medical fine-tuning improves this ability, whether its correct answers rest on sound clinical reasoning, or whether it actually uses the images it is given. We examine these questions for four open models of 8 to 27 billion parameters on the Spanish MIR residency examination, scoring 1,552 questions from eight editions under the exam's own rules. Answering every question, the three larger models would rank among roughly the first 600 to 3,000 candidates, with 41 to 43 specialties still open to them. Abstention, however, never pays, because even their least confident answers are right more often than the 25% break-even. Medical fine-tuning reduced overconfidence at the cost of accuracy, without improving how well confidence separates right from wrong answers. Moreover, 13-38% of correct answers rejected a distractor for a clinically unsound reason that confidence did not reflect, and removing or swapping the provided contextual images left accuracy unchanged.
items.title_zh: LLM 能匹配上住院医师吗？开放模型在西班牙 MIR 考试中的不确定性、推理与图像使用
items.summary: Four open models of 8 to 27 billion parameters were scored on 1,552 questions from eight editions of Spain's MIR residency exam; the three larger models would rank roughly between 600th and 3,000th, but medical fine-tuning lowered overconfidence at the cost of accuracy and removing or swapping the contextual images left accuracy unchanged.

items.title: A Sparse Topometric Graph for Scalable Cross-Session Indoor Navigation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Eun Sun Lee, Minkyun Seo, Gwangtak Bae, Junho Kim, Seunggu Kang et al.

A conventional embodied agent in an indoor environment builds a map by accumulating noisy real-world measurements and results from heavy inference to guide navigation. While the detailed measurements may differ due to scene changes or sensor settings, the unique topological structure of navigable passages or the connectivity between rooms may provide training-free guidance that complements local observations. We propose a sparse topometric graph as an efficient structural representation for robust indoor navigation, alleviating the need for fine-grained matching, which is computationally expensive, memory-intensive, and prone to real-world variations. The map consists of nodes that encode local 3D geometry and distance-weighted edges that capture traversable connectivity. A learned graph-matching network finds consistent subgraph structures across sessions by considering both node-level geometric descriptors and neighborhood connectivity. The holistic contextual matching is robust to local ambiguities caused by weak distinctiveness or repetitive structure, and establishes stable correspondences despite local scene changes, different sensor modalities, or limited spatial overlap. We analyze the practicality of the graph through cross-session point-goal navigation, where a goal specified in a prior reference map must be reached from an unknown initial pose in a later session. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest success rates (77.1% on Gibson and 40.0% under 3D-FRONT scene changes), while reducing memory by more than two orders of magnitude compared to point-level representations. The proposed approach further supports cross-session alignment and goal-directed navigation with strong scalability and robust real-world transfer.
items.title_zh: 面向可扩展跨会话室内导航的稀疏拓扑度量图
items.summary: The paper proposes a sparse topometric graph whose nodes encode local 3D geometry and whose edges capture traversable connectivity, matched across sessions by a learned graph-matching network. It reached 77.1% success on Gibson and 40.0% under 3D-FRONT scene changes while cutting memory by more than two orders of magnitude.

items.title: DLT Terms 100: a learner's glossary based on ISO 22739:2024
items.raw_content:
Authors: Yusuke Kaneko, Takumi Aita, Kohei Ichihara, Hiroki Watanabe

We propose ``DLT Terms 100'' aimed at improving literacy regarding blockchain (distributed ledger technology: DLT). The pace of DLT's social implementation has been slower than initially expected, partly due to a shortage of engineers and literate individuals. In particular, the discrepancy between business and technical terminology, and the confusion caused by the repurposing of existing financial terms, are barriers to understanding the concepts and technologies. Our proposed glossary is based on ISO 22739:2024, and categorizes and labels terms based on their frequency of appearance in representative domestic and international literature and their difficulty level.
items.title_zh: DLT Terms 100：基于 ISO 22739:2024 的学习者术语表
items.summary: The authors propose DLT Terms 100, a blockchain glossary based on ISO 22739:2024 that categorizes and labels terms by their frequency in representative domestic and international literature and by difficulty, aiming to close terminology gaps between business and engineering.

items.title: ReCoG: Relational Concept Graph for Training-Free Personalization
items.raw_content:
Authors: Changseon Yu, Hyeokjun Kweon

Training-free personalization adapts a frozen vision-language model (VLM) to recognize user-defined concepts from only a few exemplars by retrieving concept entries at inference time. While recent retriever-based methods enrich each concept with descriptive evidence, they largely treat concepts in isolation, so the retrieved information can be plausible yet non-discriminative, especially when the personalized concept set contains highly confusable, fine-grained categories. We argue that personalization is inherently relational: correct recognition depends on the specific distinctions between a concept and its nearest alternatives. To this end, we propose ReCoG, a Relational Concept Graph for retrieval-augmented personalization. ReCoG represents concepts as nodes and augments them with directed edges that explicitly capture discriminative cues between concept pairs, elicited by a frozen VLM during database construction. At inference, ReCoG retrieves a shortlist and resolves ambiguity via explicit pairwise comparisons conditioned on the corresponding relational edges, selecting the concept that consistently wins against competing candidates. We also introduce FINGER benchmark to test personalized recognition on confusable concept sets. Across FINGER, ReCoG substantially outperforms prior methods, with the largest gains in the most confusable regimes. ReCoG also achieves consistently best performance on established personalization benchmarks including captioning and VQA, confirming that relational evidence is broadly beneficial beyond fine-grained settings. Project Page: https://csy-98.github.io/ReCoG/
items.title_zh: ReCoG：面向免训练个性化的关系概念图
items.summary: ReCoG represents personalized concepts as nodes in a graph augmented with directed edges that capture discriminative cues between confusable pairs, then resolves ambiguity at inference through pairwise comparisons; it also introduces the FINGER benchmark for confusable concept sets.

items.title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs
items.raw_content:
Authors: Yifan Yuan, Yancheng Zhu, Zuoyu Zhang, Xiaogang Peng

Most automated survey generation systems retrieve papers as flat documents, limiting their ability to capture research structure. We present SurveyGraph, a framework built around a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph (MEKG) encoding method-level follow-on, competition, and shared-resource relations. The graph supports core-paper discovery, retrieval, hybrid outlining, and evidence-gated narrative synthesis. We evaluate retrieval, semantic edges, citation grounding, collection coverage, and generation-stage components. In a controlled seven-method equal-budget benchmark, MEKG-anchored fusion balances recall and structural density, with an independent co-citation check. In a separate archived graph-native diagnostic, graph-aware retrieval nearly doubles recall over flat lexical baselines across eight runs (p = 0.004). A semantic evidence gate achieves AUC = 0.75. Audits of 160 generated sentences find 80.6% anchored-or-partial citation support. Human adjudication of 108 stratified semantic edges finds 68.5% supported-or-partial relations (binary-support Cohen's kappa = 0.64), with improves strongest (80.6%) and extends weakest (52.8%). A SurveyBench-facing collection probe reaches mean reference coverage of 0.521 across four topics with an eight-paper budget. Same-backend Qwen diagnostics on a 30-paper/74-relation graph show reduced organization signals when hybrid outlining is removed. Concurrent-system comparisons provide bounded context rather than matched-backend end-to-end evidence. The results position MEKG as an auditable structural layer for typed diagnostics, relation-specific filtering, and controlled survey generation. Code and artifacts: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/SurveyGraph.
items.title_zh: SurveyGraph：通过方法—实体知识图谱生成学术综述
items.summary: SurveyGraph builds a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph encoding follow-on, competition and shared-resource relations between methods to support core-paper discovery, retrieval and evidence-gated narrative synthesis; in one diagnostic, graph-aware retrieval nearly doubled recall over flat lexical baselines.

items.title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu et al.

Single-image 3D generation has achieved high fidelity on curated benchmarks, yet degrades sharply on real-world images with uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions. Purifying such inputs requires deciding when to intervene and preserving the visual cues needed for 3D generation, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. We introduce Gate3DGen, a selective pre-processing model that gates image inputs to existing 3D generators without retraining them. A degradation-aware router bypasses inputs classified as clean and extracts features to guide purification of the remaining inputs. Conditioned on these features, a 3D-oriented one-step purifier purifies degraded inputs with spatial losses that encourage preservation of object identity, contours, and textural cues. To provide paired supervision, we construct a synthetic data engine that renders clean views of 3D assets and synthesises composite degradations. On the synthetic benchmark, the purifier improves image fidelity and downstream 3D geometry in only 2.3s on average, reducing TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% relative to degraded inputs. VLM evaluation and human preferences on real photographs further support identity preservation and degradation correction. More demos and code are available at https://supra-3d.github.io/gate3dgen.
items.title_zh: Gate3DGen：为三维生成选择性净化真实世界图像的预处理模型
items.summary: Gate3DGen is a selective pre-processing model that bypasses inputs classified as clean and purifies degraded ones before existing single-image 3D generators, using a degradation-aware router and a one-step purifier; on its synthetic benchmark it reduced TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% in about 2.3 seconds on average.
